subject: Private deployment: nodepool consolidation & IO balance for NovaHealth
messages:
From: Diego Fernandez <diego.fernandez@redwood.com>
To: Samir Shah <samir@novahealth.io>
Cc: Neha Kapoor <neha.kapoor@redwood.com>, Jordan Blake <jordan.blake@redwood.com>
Date: 2026-10-06T09:12:00-07:00
Subject: Private deployment: nodepool consolidation & IO balance for NovaHealth

Samir —

Thanks again for the time this morning. As discussed, your ops team is targeting a more consolidated nodepool layout to simplify scheduling and reduce cross-pool cold-starts while keeping IO headroom for large-batch inference jobs. I pulled together a short proposal and the IO profile export you ran last week (attached).

High-level asks from our side so we can finalize the Private deployment config: 
- Confirm whether tenant isolation must remain at pod-level (namespace) vs. strict nodepool isolation for regulatory reasons.
- Expected concurrent live-request QPS per model during peak windows (we have estimates but want to align).
- Any air-gapped requirements (certificate rotation cadence, offline KMS) that would affect bootstrap automation.

Proposal summary (attached PDF):
- Move from 4 nodepools -> 2 nodepools: compute-heavy (A100/80GB) and general-purpose (A10s/NVMe).
- General-purpose nodes use local NVMe for ephemeral KV cache with EBS-like blockstore for persistent volumes with replication across racks.
- IO guardrails: enable burst IO class for up to 2x baseline for scheduled retraining/embeddings runs; limit background batch jobs to off-peak windows.

Next steps: if the internal constraints above look OK, I’ll book a 30-min ops walkthrough to finalize PV classes and eviction policies. I’ve looped in Neha and Jordan from our deploy team.

Attachments: nodepool_consolidation_proposal_v1.pdf, nova_io_profiles_20261005.csv

—
Diego Fernandez
Solutions Engineer, Private Deployments
Redwood Inference
Mobile: +1 (415) 555-0199
From: Samir Shah <samir@novahealth.io>
To: Diego Fernandez <diego.fernandez@redwood.com>
Cc: ops-eng@novahealth.io
Date: 2026-10-06T10:04:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Private deployment: nodepool consolidation & IO balance for NovaHealth

Diego —

Thanks for the summary and the quick turnaround. A few clarifications from our side: 
1) Regulatory isolation: for PHI ingestion pipelines we need node-level tenant separation for the compliant staging cluster, but production inference can be namespace-isolated if we maintain strict egress controls.
2) Peak concurrent QPS: for the high-throughput embedding model we expect ~220 QPS sustained during a 2-hour marketing batch window, and a 35 QPS tail during normal traffic.
3) Air-gap: not required today, but we do require automated support for offline KMS sync; key rotation can be quarterly.

We reviewed the proposal PDF quickly and like the two-pool approach; main concern is the persistent volume fallback — we run nightly backups and want to ensure PV detach/reattach times won’t push jobs into cold cache windows.

Happy to take the 30-min ops walkthrough. Can you do 2pm PT today? I’ll ask ops-eng@novahealth.io to join.

—
Samir Shah
Head of Platform Engineering
NovaHealth
From: Diego Fernandez <diego.fernandez@redwood.com>
To: Samir Shah <samir@novahealth.io>
Cc: Neha Kapoor <neha.kapoor@redwood.com>, Jordan Blake <jordan.blake@redwood.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>
Date: 2026-10-06T11:15:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Private deployment: nodepool consolidation & IO balance for NovaHealth

Samir —

Perfect, appreciate the details. Quick notes inline: 
- Node-level isolation: OK — for the staging PHI tenants we’ll keep a dedicated nodepool with taints+tolerations. Production inference will use namespace isolation with hardened networkPolicies and egress enforcement at the vSwitch.
- QPS sizing: 220 QPS sustained is higher than our original estimate. That pushes the compute-heavy pool sizing from 6 -> 9 A100s for the active set to keep per-token latency under 120ms at p95 with default batching. We’ll include optional burst capacity (cold spare nodes that boot in ~90s) if you want lower commit.
- PV fallback: we recommend an N+1 attachment strategy for the blockstore controller and use local NVMe for KV cache to avoid PV detach/attach during typical evictions. The proposal includes a pvc-binding-latency table — we’ll walk it in the call.

I scheduled 2:00pm PT for the ops walkthrough and created a short shared doc with the agenda (link below). Please ping if you need a different time.

Call details: Zoom link (internal), Agenda: 1) final nodepool sizes + taints, 2) PV classes + replication SLA, 3) eviction & batch scheduling policy, 4) rollout plan + canary test.

Related links: https://drive.redwood.com/drive/folders/0B1-novahealth-nodepool-proposal

—
Diego Fernandez
Solutions Engineer, Private Deployments
Redwood Inference
From: Jordan Blake <jordan.blake@redwood.com>
To: Diego Fernandez <diego.fernandez@redwood.com>, Neha Kapoor <neha.kapoor@redwood.com>, Samir Shah <samir@novahealth.io>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>
Date: 2026-10-06T15:42:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Private deployment: nodepool consolidation & IO balance for NovaHealth

Quick notes from the rollout prep that I wanted to capture before the call: 
- Canary plan: 10% traffic on 2 nodes for 48h with observability hooks (latency, token cost, tail lat p99). If stable, ramp 10% increments every 12h.
- PV strategy: use blockstore-replicated class (sync to remote rack) for model weight PVs; GP nodes keep ephemeral NVMe cache with eviction TTL = 30m for KV.
- KMS/offline: we’ll include an offline-import script in the bootstrap to seed keys; rotation automation will run outside airgap windows and is documented in the playbook.
- Action items before call: Neha to confirm scheduler preemption thresholds; Diego to add pvc-binding-latency table to the drive doc; Marissa to approve the optional cold-spare budget for burst capacity.

Looking forward — I’ll share the meeting notes and a short decision log after the walkthrough.

—
Jordan Blake
Tech Lead, Deployments
Redwood Inference
